- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast shows a sharp downward trend, reduce the forecast’s drop magnitude — model tends to overcorrect.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.7) and forecast is rising, cap the upward momentum — model often overshoots bullish moves.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive declines or rises), model tends to lag — adjust forecast to align with recent trend direction.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overpredicts continuation — reduce forecast slope for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.3–0.6), model tends to overreact — dampen forecast volatility and favor smoother transitions.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period rallies — increase forecast toward end of horizon if sentiment turns positive mid-period.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +1 → -1 → +1), model tends to misalign with sentiment — use sentiment-weighted smoothing to reduce noise.
